source: Explicitly authorized reusable contact module; the Cardinal System wrapper and terrain implementation are excluded.
upstream_note: The original source attributes its adaptation to Anka He Chen Gaia under Apache-2.0, revision c229692. Preserve that attribution; this provenance is not independent verification of equivalence to the paper.
wormwood_changes: Optional element labels and exclusions support finite-element contact. Rooted soil currently excludes only vertices of the same tetrahedron; every distinct tetrahedron remains collidable, including cohesive neighbours.

Prescribed rigid vertices retain native force, Hessian and conservative displacement responses; a six-degree-of-freedom Newton solve uses full-spade mass/inertia, bounded hand wrench and the contact Hessian metric.

The bounded C bridge exposes forces, Hessians, bounds, element filters and accepted-pose synchronization through contracted native operations. Synchronization retains the fixed-step previous positions for friction without rebuilding unchanged topology.

This remains a CPU adaptation with independent strict crossing/inversion rejection, coarse cohesive tetrahedral material and massless tension roots. It is not a calibrated soil model or a claim of equivalence to the authors' implementation or benchmarks.

The Rust rigid solver projects optional anatomical grasp workspace and shaft-slide constraints together with native conservative contact bounds; held and released modes are explicit request data. This adds no native test-only or System-ID exception.
